What does carpet installation cost in Seattle, WA?

Plan on $4 to $7 per square foot installed in Seattle — carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away together. Most projects come in between $2,000 and $4,500; a 1,200 sq ft main floor with a staircase generally runs $5,500 to $8,500. What moves the number most is carpet grade, and you pick that from the samples we lay out in your own rooms.
Does your mobile carpet showroom cover Seattle?

It does — from Ballard bungalows to Belltown high-rises. The van carries 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades; we lay them in the rooms they'd be installed in so the color reads true where it will live, then measure everything and leave a written price the same visit. Live in a condo building? We'll sort out elevator and loading logistics with your manager. The visit is free.
What does carpet stretching cost in Seattle?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Seattle. A power stretcher pulls ripples, waves and bunched doorway edges flat again for roughly a fifth of what replacement costs — so if the pile still stands up and you still like the color, stretching is usually the smarter spend.
What do carpeted stairs cost in a Seattle home?

Stair installation starts at $18 per step, in either a waterfall wrap or a tailored cap-and-band. Older Seattle homes are full of pie-shaped turns and mid-run landings; those go into the written quote at the measure, so the final bill matches the paper.
How long will my carpet installation take?

One day covers most Seattle jobs — three or four bedrooms plus a staircase is a normal day for the crew. A whole house with heavy furniture, or a condo where the freight elevator sets the pace, can run into a second day. The schedule is written on your quote.
Will the installers move my furniture?

Yes. On most jobs the crew moves beds, couches, dressers and tables, then puts every piece back where it started. Your part is the small stuff — closet floors, electronics, lamps, breakables and anything you'd rather carry with your own hands.
Should I restretch my carpet or replace it?

If the pile stands up, the backing is sound and you still like the color, a $99-per-room stretch is usually all it needs. Replace when traffic lanes are matted flat, seams are opening, the backing is breaking down, or pet odor has outlived a professional cleaning. Send photos or book a measure and we'll tell you which side yours falls on before we quote anything.
Which Seattle neighborhoods does OC Flooring cover?

All of them. We're regularly in Ballard, Wallingford, Fremont, Green Lake, Phinney Ridge, Greenwood, Queen Anne, Magnolia, Capitol Hill, Ravenna, Maple Leaf, Wedgwood, Beacon Hill, Columbia City, Mount Baker and West Seattle — plus Shoreline, White Center, Burien and the Eastside.
Which carpet handles dogs and cats best?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, installed over a moisture-barrier pad. The barrier keeps accidents from soaking into the subfloor — the real source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber can take a diluted-bleach cleanup without losing its color. The moisture-barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What warranty do I get on the installation?

OC Flooring backs the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the carpet carries the mill's wear-and-stain warranty on top — usually 10 to 25 years depending on grade. Both are spelled out on your written quote. Pad choice can affect mill coverage, which is one more reason all three pad grades ride along on the visit.
